item.description: The AI Engineer World’s Fair ended with a debate about loops, a report on the state of AI engineering, and closing keynotes focused on what to build next.

item.title: Vercel's Andrew Qu on why agents are a new kind of software
item.description: The Vercel Chief of Software explains how its agent framework, eve, was created — and why skills, sandboxes and agent-readable websites now matter.

item.title: The website of the future may assemble itself for every visitor
item.description: Adobe is experimenting with “agentic sites” that generate pages around an individual user’s intent. At AIEWF, we talked to Carlos Sanchez about the Web's future.

item.title: Skill engineering and the case against one-shot AI design
item.description: Paul Bakaus talks to us about Impeccable, human judgment in a 'loopmaxxing' era, and why agents still need people to steer them.

item.title: AIEWF Daily Dispatch: Autoresearch and the tension between AI and human agency
item.description: The software factory vision met resistance today from speakers defending human understanding and control.

item.title: Autoresearch: The feedback loop behind self-improving agents
item.description: Introspection co-founder Roland Gavrilescu explains autoresearch, agent “recipes,” self-improving loops, and why humans remain central to the software factory.

item.title: How Cursor deploys AI inside the enterprise
item.description: Cursor's Pauline Brunet explains how her team of Forward Deployed Engineers help organizations implement agents — essentially setting up software factories.

item.title: 🔬 The Coolest Diffusion Research Isn't in LLMs — Evan Feinberg & Sergey Edunov, Genesis Molecular AI
item.description: Why the Llama lead left Meta for drug discovery, PEARL's zero-shot OpenBind win, and what becomes possible when co-folding finally crosses the accuracy threshold.

item.title: Warp CEO Zach Lloyd on why software factories are the next phase of coding
item.description: Warp's founder thinks every major software project will soon run on an automated factory. He discusses why and how engineers should prepare for this shift.
